notice: Curated demonstration dataset covering India. Coordinates are published figures rounded to four decimal places, not a field survey, and every record carries the source it came from. These are not user contributions and none of the records has been field-verified.

sites.name: Taj Mahal
sites.description: A white-marble mausoleum commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal, completed in the 17th century and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

sites.name: Agra Fort
sites.description: A walled Mughal fort beside the Yamuna in Agra, developed under Akbar and later emperors and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

sites.name: Fatehpur Sikri
sites.description: The short-lived Mughal capital founded by Akbar in the 16th century, with palace, mosque and civic buildings, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

sites.name: Sarnath
sites.description: A Buddhist archaeological site near Varanasi where the Buddha is said to have preached his first sermon; the Dhamek Stupa and monastic remains are the principal monuments.

sites.name: Qutub Minar
sites.description: A fluted sandstone minaret begun under Qutb al-Din Aibak and completed by later rulers, surrounded by the Qutub complex and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

sites.name: Red Fort
sites.description: The Mughal palace fort of Shah Jahan in Old Delhi, built in the 17th century and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.

sites.name: Humayun's Tomb
sites.description: A 16th-century Mughal garden tomb in Delhi, the first of its kind on the subcontinent and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

sites.name: Jama Masjid, Delhi
sites.description: One of the largest mosques in India, built in the 17th century under Shah Jahan opposite the Red Fort in Old Delhi.

sites.name: Golden Temple
sites.description: The Harmandir Sahib, the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism, founded in the 16th century in Amritsar and rebuilt several times; its upper storeys are gilded.

sites.name: Jallianwala Bagh
sites.description: A memorial garden in Amritsar marking the site of the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre during the colonial period.

sites.name: Sheikh Chilli's Tomb
sites.description: A Mughal-era tomb complex at Thanesar in Kurukshetra, associated with the Sufi saint Sheikh Chilli and set within a walled garden.

sites.name: Capitol Complex, Chandigarh
sites.description: Le Corbusier's legislative and administrative ensemble in Chandigarh, part of the transnational inscription "The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier" (2016).

sites.name: Jaisalmer Fort
sites.description: A living desert fort founded in the 12th century, part of the UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscription (2013), with Jain temples and densely built housing inside its walls.

sites.name: Amer Fort
sites.description: A hill-top palace fort near Jaipur with courtyards, gardens and mirrored halls, part of the UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscription (2013).

sites.name: Hawa Mahal
sites.description: An 18th-century palace facade in Jaipur with a honeycomb of small windows, built so that the royal women could observe street life unseen.

sites.name: Kumbhalgarh
sites.description: A Mewar hill fort in the Aravallis with long defensive walls, part of the UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscription (2013).

sites.name: Rani ki Vav
sites.description: A seven-storey stepwell in Patan built in the 11th century and attributed to Queen Udayamati, silted over by the Saraswati and rediscovered in the 20th century; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014.

sites.name: Adalaj Stepwell
sites.description: A five-storey stepwell in Adalaj village near Gandhinagar, dated by inscription to 1499 and associated with Ruda Devi, with carved sandstone panels.

sites.name: Sun Temple, Modhera
sites.description: A Sun temple at Modhera attributed to Bhima I of the Chaulukya dynasty, with a stepped tank (Surya Kund), a pillared hall and a carved shrine.

sites.name: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
sites.description: A archaeological park around the fortified city of Champaner and the sacred hill of Pavagadh, with fortifications, mosques, temples and water structures; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004.

sites.name: Dholavira
sites.description: A major Indus (Harappan) city on Khadir Bet in Kutch with a citadel, middle town and lower town, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

sites.name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
sites.description: A group of Chandela-era Hindu and Jain temples known for their sculpted facades, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

sites.name: Sanchi Stupa
sites.description: A Buddhist monumental complex begun under Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, with stupas, gateways and monastic remains; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989.

sites.name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
sites.description: A group of sandstone rock shelters with prehistoric paintings, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.

sites.name: Orchha Fort Complex
sites.description: The palace and temple complex of the Bundela rulers beside the Betwa river, including the Jahangir Mahal and Raj Mahal.

sites.name: Sirpur Monuments
sites.description: An archaeological complex on the Mahanadi with brick temples and Buddhist remains from the Panduvamshi period, including the Laxman Temple.

sites.name: Ajanta Caves
sites.description: Buddhist rock-cut caves with paintings and sculpture in the Sahyadri hills, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

sites.name: Ellora Caves
sites.description: A rock-cut cave complex near Aurangabad with Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments, including the Kailasa temple; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.

sites.name: Elephanta Caves
sites.description: Rock-cut Shaiva caves on an island in Mumbai Harbour, known for the monumental Trimurti sculpture; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

sites.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
sites.description: A Victorian Gothic railway terminus in Mumbai, opened in the 19th century and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004.

sites.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
sites.description: A Baroque church in Old Goa holding the tomb of St Francis Xavier, part of the UNESCO inscription "Churches and Convents of Goa" (1986).

sites.name: Hampi
sites.description: The ruined capital of the Vijayanagara empire on the Tungabhadra, with temples, bazaars and royal enclosures; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986.

sites.name: Pattadakal
sites.description: A group of Chalukya-era Hindu and Jain temples on the Malaprabha, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

sites.name: Mysore Palace
sites.description: The royal palace of the Wadiyar dynasty in Mysuru, rebuilt in the late 19th and early 20th centuries in an Indo-Saracenic style.

sites.name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
sites.description: A Vishnu temple in Thiruvananthapuram with a monumental gopuram and pillared corridors, expanded by the Travancore rulers.

sites.name: Mattancherry Palace
sites.description: A 16th-century palace in Kochi built by the Portuguese and later modified by the Dutch, known for its murals and now a museum.

sites.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
sites.description: An 11th-century Chola temple in Thanjavur with a monumental vimana, part of the UNESCO inscription "Great Living Chola Temples" (1987).

sites.name: Mahabalipuram Group of Monuments
sites.description: A coastal group of Pallava rock-cut temples, rathas and reliefs, including the Shore Temple; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

sites.name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
sites.description: A large Dravidian temple complex in Madurai dedicated to Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, with tall gopurams and pillared halls largely built in the 16th and 17th centuries.

sites.name: Charminar
sites.description: A four-minaret gateway and mosque in Hyderabad built in the 16th century under Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, at the heart of the old city.

sites.name: Golconda Fort
sites.description: A hill fort and former Qutb Shahi capital west of Hyderabad, known for its gates, bastions and acoustic architecture.

sites.name: Lepakshi
sites.description: A Vijayanagara-era temple complex at Lepakshi known for its hanging pillar, murals and the large Nandi monolith.

sites.name: Sun Temple, Konark
sites.description: A 13th-century Sun temple conceived as a monumental chariot with carved wheels and horses; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

sites.name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
sites.description: A major Vaishnava temple in Puri dedicated to Jagannath, built in the 12th century and the focus of the annual Rath Yatra.

sites.name: Victoria Memorial
sites.description: A marble memorial building and museum in Kolkata completed in the early 20th century, set in a large garden.

sites.name: Bishnupur Temples
sites.description: A group of brick temples at Bishnupur faced with terracotta panels, built under the Malla rulers in the 17th and 18th centuries.

sites.name: Mahabodhi Temple
sites.description: The Buddhist temple complex at Bodh Gaya marking the place of the Buddha's enlightenment, with the Mahabodhi tree; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002.

sites.name: Nalanda Mahavihara
sites.description: The excavated remains of the ancient Buddhist monastic university at Nalanda, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

sites.name: Maluti Temples
sites.description: A cluster of small brick temples at Maluti in Dumka district, decorated with terracotta panels and dated to the 17th–19th centuries.

sites.name: Kamakhya Temple
sites.period: 8th century CE onwards; present structure rebuilt
sites.description: A Shakti temple on Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, an important pilgrimage site whose present structure was rebuilt in the 16th–17th centuries.

sites.name: Charaideo Moidams
sites.description: The royal burial mounds (moidams) of the Ahom dynasty at Charaideo, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024.

sites.name: Nongriat Living Root Bridges
sites.description: Bridges formed from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees by Khasi communities near Nongriat; a living tradition rather than a single dated monument, so no historical period is asserted here.

sites.name: Kangla Fort
sites.description: The historic royal seat of the Meitei kings at Imphal, with earthwork defences, shrines and palace remains.

sites.name: Vangchhia Menhirs
sites.description: An archaeological site in Champhai district with standing stones, rock-cut channels and terraces; its chronology is not confidently dated in the sources consulted, so no period is asserted.

sites.name: Kohima War Cemetery
sites.description: A Commonwealth war cemetery at Kohima commemorating the 1944 Battle of Kohima during the Second World War.

sites.name: Unakoti
sites.description: A hillside site of rock-cut reliefs and monolithic figures in Tripura, traditionally dated to the 8th–9th centuries.

sites.name: Rumtek Monastery
sites.description: A Kagyu monastery near Gangtok with 16th-century origins, rebuilt in the 1960s as the seat of the Karmapa in exile.

sites.name: Tawang Monastery
sites.description: A large Gelug monastery founded in the 17th century in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh, and one of the largest monasteries in India.

sites.name: Martand Sun Temple
sites.description: The ruined 8th-century Sun temple at Martand in the Kashmir Valley, built under the Karkota dynasty and notable for its colonnaded courtyard.

sites.name: Raghunath Temple
sites.description: A 19th-century temple complex in Jammu with a series of shrines and a tall gateway, built under the Dogra rulers.

sites.name: Leh Palace
sites.description: The 17th-century former royal palace above Leh, built under the Namgyal dynasty and now a museum and viewpoint.

sites.name: Cellular Jail
sites.description: A colonial-era prison in Port Blair used to detain political prisoners, now a national memorial.

sites.name: Ujra Mosque, Kavaratti
sites.description: A historic mosque on Kavaratti island known for its carved wooden and coral work; the sources consulted do not give a secure construction date, so no period is asserted.

sites.name: Pondicherry French Quarter
sites.description: The grid of colonial-era streets and townhouses in the former French quarter of Puducherry, shaped by French administration from the 18th century.

sites.name: Diu Fort
sites.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
sites.description: A 16th-century Portuguese sea fort on the island of Diu, with bastions, a lighthouse and a chapel.

sites.name: Har Ki Pauri
sites.description: A historic bathing ghat on the Ganges at Haridwar and one of the city's principal ritual sites; its present form results from successive rebuilds rather than a single dated construction.

sites.name: Kangra Fort
sites.description: A hill fort above the Kangra valley associated with the Katoch dynasty, with earlier origins and substantial later rebuilding.
